review.aidoc.faq.1.answer.aidocs.fda.cle: Aidoc's FDA-cleared algorithms detect time-critical conditions across 11+ specialties including intracranial hemorrhage, large vessel occlusion (stroke), pulmonary embolism, cervical spine fractures, rib fractures, incidental pulmonary embolism, pneumothorax, and other acute pathologies. The platform focuses specifically on life-threatening or time-sensitive findings that require immediate clinical intervention. Additional algorithms are continuously being developed and validated for new conditions and specialties.
review.aidoc.faq.2.answer.aidoc.provides: Aidoc provides real-time analysis, typically delivering alerts within minutes of scan completion. The platform processes studies as they're acquired, analyzing images during reconstruction. When critical findings are detected, push notifications are sent immediately to configured smartphones and devices. Studies show Aidoc reduces time from scan completion to radiologist notification by 60-80% compared to standard workflows, enabling faster treatment initiation for time-sensitive emergencies like stroke and trauma.
Yes, Aidoc has received FDA 510(k) clearance for multiple algorithms including intracranial hemorrhage detection, cervical spine fracture detection, pulmonary embolism detection, and other indications. Each algorithm undergoes rigorous clinical validation and regulatory review before clearance. Aidoc also has CE marking for use in Europe. The platform meets regulatory requirements as a medical device for clinical diagnostic support and is deployed in compliance with HIPAA and other healthcare data protection regulations.
review.aidoc.faq.4.answer.no.aidoc.is.de: No, Aidoc is designed to assist radiologists, not replace them. The platform serves as a triage and prioritization tool that flags urgent cases requiring immediate attention. Radiologists remain responsible for final diagnosis, clinical reporting, and patient care decisions. Aidoc's value is in ensuring critical findings don't get delayed in busy workflows and providing a safety net against oversight. Studies show AI-assisted radiology combining Aidoc's triage with radiologist expertise delivers optimal patient outcomes compared to either alone.
review.aidoc.faq.5.question.what.infrast: What infrastructure is needed for Aidoc?
review.aidoc.faq.5.answer.aidoc.requires: Aidoc requires integration with your hospital's PACS system to receive imaging studies and deliver results. The platform can be deployed cloud-based or on-premise depending on your security and performance requirements. Cloud deployment needs reliable internet for study upload and result delivery. You'll also need smartphones or mobile devices for clinicians to receive push notifications. Aidoc's implementation team provides technical support for PACS integration with major vendors including GE, Philips, Siemens, and others. Implementation typically takes several weeks to months depending on complexity.
review.aidoc.faq.6.answer.aidoc.uses.cus: Aidoc uses custom enterprise pricing based on hospital size, scan volumes, selected algorithms, and deployment configuration. Pricing models typically include annual licensing fees with options for per-study charges or unlimited usage. Costs generally range from hundreds of thousands to over a million dollars annually for large health systems. The investment includes software licensing, PACS integration, mobile app access, ongoing technical support, and algorithm updates. Many hospitals report strong ROI through improved patient outcomes, reduced liability from missed findings, and enhanced operational efficiency. Contact Aidoc directly for pricing tailored to your organization's specific requirements.
